headline: EU Commission reported to scrap Green Claims Directive amid regulatory updates
summary: The European Commission reportedly plans to scrap the Green Claims Directive, potentially easing ex-ante verification burdens for consumer marketing. Meanwhile, analyses clarify CSRD and CSDDD thresholds under the Omnibus package, and national implementations of the Pay Transparency Directive advance ahead of upcoming corporate reporting and product compliance milestones.

items.title: EU Commission reportedly plans to abandon Green Claims Directive
items.what: Media reports indicate the European Commission intends to withdraw the proposed Green Claims Directive, abandoning plans for mandatory third-party pre-approval of environmental claims.
items.meaning: Eases expected administrative burdens for consumer marketing on your brand's tools, though existing national unfair commercial practices laws still apply.
items.action: Continue substantiating environmental marketing claims while awaiting official confirmation from the European Commission.

sources.title: EU Commission Abandons Plans For The Green Claims Directive

items.title: Omnibus Reform analysis clarifies CSRD and CSDDD obligations
items.what: Legal analysis outlined updated sustainability reporting and due diligence expectations following the EU Omnibus reform package.
items.meaning: Confirms your CSRD reporting obligations start from FY2027, while your headcount keeps you outside the direct scope of the CSDDD.
items.action: Align Chinese supplier sustainability data collection with CSRD metrics rather than CSDDD due diligence protocols.

sources.title: ESG disclosure and corporate due diligence obligations under the Omnibus Reform

items.title: EUDR compliance preparations advance with updated guidance and training
items.what: Third-country training and updated industry guidance were published to support compliance with EU Deforestation Regulation traceability standards.
items.meaning: Affects wooden handles, paper packaging or cardboard imported with your finished products ahead of the December 2026 application date.
items.action: Ensure Chinese suppliers of wood components and packaging are prepared to provide geolocation traceability data.

sources.title: Training on wood traceability according to EUDR standards.

items.title: Pay transparency implementation mandates salary ranges in job ads
items.what: EU Member States are introducing legislation under the Pay Transparency Directive requiring salary ranges in job advertisements next year.
items.meaning: Directly impacts HR processes for your EU headcount, requiring published salary bands and internal pay structure reviews.
items.action: Review recruitment practices and establish formal salary structures across all EU operations.
